OBS Studio 33 (beta)

Recording and streaming

Patched

Screen recording and live streaming. Omnix builds OBS from its own fork's master: upstream master plus Omnix's fixes, synced from time to time.

PatchedTested 2026-10-06x86_64-linux

Test run ↗
Package source

omnix-apps/obs-studio fork · master · GPL-2.0 · Website

Install
Use Omnix's OBS (flake overlay)
# flake.nix: inputs.omnix.url = "github:Omnix-Linux/Omnix";
nixpkgs.overlays = [ omnix.overlays.default ];
programs.obs-studio.enable = true;   # now Omnix's OBS from the fork
Verified workflow
  1. Build OBS from omnix-apps/obs-studio master (cb73236): upstream master plus Omnix's shutdown and core-module-path fixes
  2. obs --version runs
  3. Start OBS in an X11 session; OpenGL loads (Mesa llvmpipe in the VM)
  4. The main window maps and OBS is still running 15 s later; take a screenshot
  5. OBS's output shows every core module loading (x264, FFmpeg, PipeWire, X11 capture, browser, ...)
  6. Quit OBS through the window manager: it must exit with Result=success and leave no core dump
Validation details
Test
Omnix-Linux/Omnix/tests/apps-gui.nixnix build github:Omnix-Linux/Omnix#checks.x86_64-linux.app-obs
Last run
Patched on 2026-10-06Revision: Omnix-Linux/Omnix@cfca01dFresh NixOS VM run of OBS 33.0.0-beta6 built from omnix-apps/obs-studio master (Omnix-Linux/Omnix#8; the fork now lives in the omnix-apps organization, Omnix-Linux/Omnix#9). The fork carries two Omnix fixes: a guard against a freed core on shutdown (proposed upstream as obsproject/obs-studio#13906), and absolute core module paths on Linux, without which OBS 33 loaded no modules when built by Nix. The test requires every core module to load and a clean exit. The shutdown crash was a race, so a clean exit shows the patched build shuts down correctly; it can't prove the race never occurs.

OpenCut 0.3.0

Video editor

Passing

Open-source browser video editor (Next.js), built from its v0.3.0 source, served locally and opened in Brave.

PassingTested 2026-10-06x86_64-linux

Test run ↗
Package source

GitHub source (tag) · v0.3.0 · MIT · Website

Install
Build and run from source
git clone --branch v0.3.0 https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut && cd OpenCut
bun install && cp apps/web/.env.example apps/web/.env.local
cd apps/web && bun run build && bun run start   # then open http://localhost:3000
Verified workflow
  1. Fetch the OpenCut v0.3.0 source tag from GitHub (no Linux binary, AppImage, flake or nixpkgs package exists); bun dependencies pinned by output hash
  2. Build the Next.js app offline in Nix (next/font's Google Fonts download answered with Next's mock hook and the nixpkgs Inter font)
  3. Start OpenCut's own standalone server on 127.0.0.1:3000 with the upstream .env.example placeholders; /projects returns the app
  4. Open /editor in Brave's official Linux build in an X11 session (--no-sandbox as root, software GL via SwiftShader since the VM has no GPU)
  5. The editor creates a new project and redirects to /editor/<uuid>; the welcome dialog shows
  6. Dismiss it: the editor (assets, preview, properties, timeline) shows "Untitled Project"; take a screenshot
Validation details
Test
Omnix-Linux/Omnix/tests/apps-opencut.nixnix build github:Omnix-Linux/Omnix#checks.x86_64-linux.app-opencut
Last run
Passing on 2026-10-06Revision: Omnix-Linux/Omnix@3f1ce17Fresh NixOS VM run (nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.app-opencut) on the Omnix base with its desktop preset; the screenshot above is from this run. OpenCut publishes only the web app's source (its v0.3.0 release has no assets; nixpkgs has no package; no flake), so the test builds it from source. The editor's renderer needs WebGL2 or WebGPU: in the GPU-less VM Brave needs --use-angle=swiftshader --enable-unsafe-swiftshader, without which it shows "Failed to load project". The editor gates viewports under 1024 px, so the VM screen is 1280x800. Icon: OpenCut's own logo (apps/web/public/logos/opencut/icon.svg, MIT). Test in Omnix main (Omnix-Linux/Omnix#6).

Principles

How an app earns its place

  1. Tested, not claimed

    An app is listed for the workflow a test runs, not for a line in a feature list.

  2. Every status links to a test

    Passing, patched, known gap and failing all point at the NixOS test file and the commit it ran against. The page build refuses a status without one.

  3. Re-run after every update

    When Omnix, nixpkgs or the app changes, an agent re-runs the test and records the new result, so you can see whether a workflow that worked yesterday still works after the upgrade.

  4. Rollback when an update breaks one

    A failing workflow is a reason to stay on, or boot back to, the previous generation until it is fixed.

  5. Agent-maintained

    An agent adds an app by writing a test and a registry entry, running it, and recording the result. No hand-edited badges.

  6. No special packaging

    Apps run as unmodified upstream binaries through the Omnix standard filesystem layer: /lib64, /usr/lib, ldconfig and envfs.
